items: Fixed: the Settings modal was unusable on narrow phone screens - the connection-mode and proxy routing-mode pickers crammed long descriptions into columns as narrow as 100px; they now stack into a single column below tablet width.

Fixed: on/off switches (Memory, Run code, proxy routing, etc.) rendered as circles instead of pill-shaped toggles on mobile, because a touch-target sizing rule was overriding their height; they now keep their intended shape while buttons that need a full touch target still get one.

Fixed: small icon buttons in Settings (remove provider, accept/reject/forget memory, export/import proxies) were inflated to oversized touch targets on mobile and threw their rows out of alignment; they stay compact again, and the memory "forget" button - previously visible only on hover - now shows up on mobile too.
Fixed: the model picker sat flush against the screen edge on mobile with no breathing room; it now matches the spacing used by every other dialog.

Fixed: tapping a citation badge on mobile immediately navigated away instead of showing the source preview, since touch devices have no hover; tapping now opens the preview like hovering does on desktop, and tapping outside it closes it.

New installs now come pre-seeded with every keyless provider and a starter pool of free proxies, so free models work right away without manual setup; proxy discovery runs on a schedule server-side instead of per-client, backed by a shared Redis-cached catalog, with a master switch to turn proxy routing off entirely.
"Run code" and the built-in plugin tools are now enabled by default in Settings instead of requiring opt-in.
Renamed the "OmniRoute" connection mode to "Self-Hosted Gateway" for clarity - existing gateway connections migrate automatically and keep working.

Site analytics now require your explicit consent via a bottom bar before Google Analytics loads at all - no tracking script or cookie until you accept, and there is exactly one place to answer instead of two.

Fixed: a proxied chat reply could arrive all at once at the end of the turn instead of streaming - three separate causes are fixed: the CDN in front of the relay was buffering the response, the SSE parser didn't handle the CRLF line endings some providers use, and the tunnel's own flow control could stall delivery.

Every fenced code block a model generates now becomes a real file artifact in the side panel; mermaid, LaTeX and chart blocks render correctly instead of turning into generic code files, and a chart still renders even if the model forgets to fence it.
Fixed a bug where a reply that produced no visible content could be dropped entirely instead of showing what did come through.

The proxy relay is more reliable under real concurrent load: it sheds requests cleanly at capacity instead of degrading, reports the actual reason a connection failed instead of a generic error, and tracks rate limits per user instead of a single shared platform-wide budget.

Running JavaScript or TypeScript code can now import real npm packages (fetched from esm.sh the first time, then cached) and most Node built-ins - fs, path, crypto, http/https, events, util, buffer, and more - instead of failing with "this sandbox has no npm or Node module resolution." Only raw sockets/processes (net, dns, child_process, ...) still aren't available.

Store → Packages is now a browsable, read-only list grouped by runtime, with a real description of what each package does and a link to its PyPI page - packages already install themselves the moment your code imports them, so the Install button was just extra friction.

Fixed for real this time: attaching an image and asking about it still failed through a configured proxy after the previous fix - the size limit was on the relay's own connection to the proxy, not the upload to the relay. Large payloads are now split on both hops.
Fixed: the "Drop to attach" overlay didn't line up with the composer - it now traces the message box exactly.
Dragging an unsupported file over the composer turns the drop zone red, and dropping it anyway shakes the box and refuses the attach instead of silently adding a failed one.
Fixed: attaching an image and asking about it always failed once a proxy was configured - a large upload was tripping a size limit on the relay tunnel that a normal text message never came close to.
Fixed: a "this deployment has no proxy relay" error could appear even on a deployment that has one, when its server was just briefly unreachable.
Generate image, Edit image and Generate video now grey themselves out when none of your configured models can actually do the job, instead of opening a panel with nothing behind it.
Drag a file straight onto the composer to attach it - the paperclip menu still works too.
Fixed: "auto" claimed it could see images, watch video, reason, and call tools even with nothing configured for any of that - it now only claims what your actual models support.

Fixed: one unhealthy proxy or relay used to burn through all 12 model attempts on a single image question, each failing the exact same way; it now retries once, then tells you plainly to check your proxy settings instead of listing a wall of near-identical errors.
Large screenshots are compressed harder before upload (while keeping real transparency intact), to cut down on failures with providers or proxies that cap request size.
Charts. Ask for one and you get a real chart with hover values, drawn from the data rather than described in prose. Every chart also shows its numbers as a table and exports them as CSV.
Tables you can use: click a column to sort, numbers line up in columns, long tables keep their header in view, and any table exports to CSV.

Diagrams and maths now get offered. Timelines, flowcharts, sequence and gantt diagrams and typeset formulas already rendered here, but nothing told the assistant so - it only used them by luck. Now it knows.
Code blocks in chat are now files. Run, edit, download or copy one without leaving the message, with the output right underneath it.
Edits to a code block are kept with the conversation, so a snippet you fixed is still fixed when you come back to it.
Python can now import third-party libraries. pandas, numpy, matplotlib and the rest download the first time you run code that needs them, and work offline after that.
New Packages tab in the Store, once the Python runtime is installed: browse every library this build can install and add them ahead of time.
Fixed: a failed runtime download was quietly retried, so you waited twice as long before seeing what went wrong.
Initial release.
